correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the determinant derivative 2adj(A)_{ij}; for corank one its vanishing is equivalent to coordinate-supported kernel and a zero row, and for corank at least two all derivatives vanish. Irreducibility and dimension of the rank-at-most-n−2 section follow from the irreducible product of isotropic quadrics (dimension at least two) and generic orthogonal-group fibers; the n row spaces each have a rank-n−1 dense open. Schur complements and the absence of coordinate vectors in the two-dimensional kernel give rank-three normal quadrics on the rank-drop component; a block determinant gives invertible rank-(n−1) transverse form on row-zero components. Smooth witness and singular codimension >=2 yield irreducibility, normality and Gorenstein property. Exact independent integer checks verify derivatives and Hessian ranks for n=5,6, but do not substitute for the general proof. Limits: n>=5, algebraically closed k, char k !=2, reduced singular locus only.

value.rationale: The all-order singular classification explains a non-generic linear-section phenomenon: forcing all diagonal entries to zero creates precisely n extra maximal singular components while preserving the irreducible rank-drop component. Their dimensions and two different transverse quadratic ranks distinguish geometry that generic determinantal rank strata and standard cofactor criteria alone do not classify. This has natural use for weighted complete-graph adjacency determinants and the geometry of sparse symmetric hypersurfaces; it is not an arbitrary finite slice or routine numerical increment.
